tools_as_sent.name: channel_ask_template
tools_as_sent.description: Ask a person's manager whether they agree to a grant, when only the manager can say: the group needs the manager's agreement, or the request was made on someone else's behalf. Our code writes the question from a fixed template and sends it to the manager from the directory; you name the case. Then end your turn: the manager's reply comes later, on the returned thread, as their words, not the operator's. A YES there still does not grant anything by itself. Returns the thread to wait on.

template.description: manager_confirm: ask the manager to agree to this person getting this group.

employee_id.description: The person who would get the group. An employee ID, SYN-EMP- and four digits, such as SYN-EMP-9001.

group_id.description: A group ID, SYN-GRP- and its name, such as SYN-GRP-EXAMPLE-WRITE.

request_id.description: A request ID, SYN-REQ- and four digits, such as SYN-REQ-9001.

tools_as_sent.name: directory_get_employee
tools_as_sent.description: Read one person's directory record: name, email, department, title, role, manager (ID and name), employment, status (active, leaver or pending_start) and contract end date. Give exactly one of employee_id, email or name, and null for the other two. A name must match one person; if it matches several or none, the error lists who matched. To search more loosely, use directory_search_employees. An unknown ID is an error that names the closest people. At most 4,000 characters come back; a longer result says it was cut.

employee_id.description: An employee ID, SYN-EMP- and four digits, such as SYN-EMP-9001. Or null.

email.description: A work email, such as cleo.vance@syn-corp.example. Or null.

name.description: A person's full name, such as Cleo Vance. Or null.

tools_as_sent.name: policy_check_access
tools_as_sent.description: Ask the role policy whether one person may have each of up to 20 groups, in one call. Each decision is birthright or allowed (you may grant it), needs_manager (only a proposed change, for the operator), or forbidden, with the reason. An unknown group ID is an error that names the closest groups, and nothing is checked. Example, a typical call: {"employee_id": "SYN-EMP-9001", "group_ids": ["SYN-GRP-EXAMPLE-READ"]}. The less usual case: {"employee_id": "SYN-EMP-9001", "group_ids": ["SYN-GRP-EXAMPLE-READ", "SYN-GRP-EXAMPLE-WRITE", "SYN-GRP-EXAMPLE-ADMIN"]}.

employee_id.description: An employee ID, SYN-EMP- and four digits, such as SYN-EMP-9001.

group_ids.description: One to 20 group IDs, such as ["SYN-GRP-EXAMPLE-READ", "SYN-GRP-EXAMPLE-WRITE"].

probe.asked: Call policy_check_access once, for SYN-EMP-0052 and the group SYN-GRP-GITHUB-ENGINEERS (the GitHub engineers group).
